newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democracy leader says willing to risk jail.
newsitem.headline: HK democracy leader says willing to risk jail.

text.p: Democracy leader Martin Lee said on Tuesday he was ready to risk jail by scaling the walls of the colony's legislative council building if Beijing blocked protests on the night the British colony returns to China.
Lee, chairman of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, plans a protest on June 30 night to denounce a new Beijing-appointed legislature.
The group wants to read a pro-democracy statement from the outside balcony of the chamber, the first challenge to the right to protest once China formally takes control of the colony an hour earlier.
The incoming administration of former shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa has kept open its options on how it will handle the first challenge to its authority.

Asked if his party had applied for permission to protest, Lee told reporters: "We have not. Because it is going to be a peaceful demonstration and I don't think the Tung Government will do anything silly by blocking our way."
"If so, we may then have to climb up to the balcony with a ladder or something. I don't think the Tung government will like to see that," Lee said.

Lee, once courted by China for his anti-colonial views -- he was consulted when Beijing drafted Hong Kong's post-colonial constitution -- has since been denounced as a subversive for his pro-democracy activities.
One of Hong Kong's most prominent lawyers, he said he believes he could face jail in the future.
"The question is the police may not give us permission to protest, then we will be breaking the laws and then what?" said Lee. "We may be prosecuted and we may be put in prison."
"If there is a fine, my people will not pay it. There will be civil disobedience. The prospect of imprisonment is not impossible," he added.
Lee has spearheaded a campaign at home and abroad against the Beijing-appointed provisional legislature, which will rule Hong Kong with Tung.
He called the legislature a puppet chamber.
"It is not Hong Kong people running Hong Kong it is puppets appointed by China ruling Hong Kong. It can all be summed up in one word: Control," Lee said.
"China is putting a noose around the neck of the goose so the goose cannot be free but China still expects the goose to lay the golden egg."
